FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Construction Plant and Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering 
Division Council. 
This Indian Standard was first published in 1979. The first revision has been taken up to keep pace with the latest 
technological developments and international practices. In this revision, the following major changes have been 
made: 

a) The scope of the standard has been modified; and 

b) Clause 9 regarding marking has been added. 
Particulars regarding information to be given to the manufacturer by the purchaser with enquiry or order and the 
information to be furnished by the manufacturer to the purchaser along with the quotation are given in Annex A 
and B respectively. 
The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex D. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 9309 : 2022 


Indian Standard 
SPECIFICATION FOR ROLL CRUSHER 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard covers the design and supply of roll 
crushers which are commonly used for crushing rocks, 
minerals, coke, coal and similar materials. 


2 NOMENCLATURE AND TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the various components 
of the roll crusher shall be as designated in Fig. 1. 


2.1 Roll Crusher — A machine for crushing rocks, 
minerals, coal, coke and similar materials, mainly by 
compression between two rotating cylindrical surfaces 
rotating towards each other; or one stationary surface 
(either curved or straight) and one rotating cylindrical 
surface; or three rotating cylindrical surfaces so 
arranged that material to be crushed passes between 
any two rotating cylindrical surfaces at one time. 


3 CLASSIFICATION 
For the purpose of this standard, the roll crusher shall 


be classified as follows. 
3.1 Classification Depending Upon the Roll Surface 


Depending upon the type of roll surface, a roll crusher 
may be of smooth, beaded, spoked or corrugated roll 


type. 

3.1.1 Smooth Roll Crusher 

A crushing machine where the roll or rolls surfaces are 
smooth. 

3.1.2 Beaded Roll Crusher 


A crushing machine where the roll surface is beaded. 


3.1.3 Spiked or Toothed Roll Crusher 


A crushing machine where the roll surface is composed 
of spikes or teeth (of different shapes and sizes based 
on individual manufacturer’s design), made up by the 
combination of circular rings or longitudinally curved 
sectors carrying such spikes or teeth. 


3.1.4 Corrugated Roll Crusher 


Acrushing machine where the roll surface is corrugated. 
It can comprise of one corrugated and one smooth roll 
surface or both the roll surfaces corrugated. 


3.2 Classification Depending Upon Number of 
Rotating Rolls 


Depending upon the number of rolls the crusher may be 
single, double or triple. 


3.2.1 Single Roll Crusher 


A crusher having a single roll that rotates towards a 
stationary surface (see Fig. 1). The roll or rolls may be 
made up of crushing rings of different shapes and sizes 
based on individual design and the specific application. 
The stationary surface may be plain or of toothed design, 
straight or curved. 


3.2.2 Double Roll Crusher 


A crusher having two rolls rotating towards each other 
(see Fig. 2). 


3.2.3 Triple Roll Crusher 


A crusher having a rotating roll (of same or different 
diameter) so arranged that material to be crushed passes 
between one set of two such rolls at one time or is 
composed of a single and double roll crusher. 


4 PRINCIPLE OF OPERATION 


The raw material is crushed by one, two or three rolls, 
the feed size restricted by the angle of nip. 


4.1 The feed lump size is governed by the roll diameter 
since a certain angle of the nip should not be exceeded. If 
feed size larger than the specified one is fed, the material 
may simply ride on roll surface and thereby cause 
choking. 


4.2 Furthermore, a certain degree of reduction to match 
the characteristics of the feed material is adhered to and 
the peripheral speed of roll is matched with the crushing 
process. Consequently, feet size, roll diameter and 
length, roll speed, roll setting determine the output.

5 CONSTRUCTION 


The roll crusher shall comprise of the following parts 
(see Fig. 1 and 2): 


a) Base frame; 

b) Roll assembly; 

c) Drive unit; 

d) Cover; 

e) Roll gap adjustment and safety device; 

f) Feeding device and discharge chutes; 

g) Attachment for maintenance of rolls; and 
h) Electric motor/prime mover. 


The various parts mentioned above shall conform to the 
requirements given in 5.1 to 5.7. 


5.1 Base Frame 


It shall serve the purpose of supporting the rolls, 
housing, adjustment assembly, and the drive motor/ 
prime movers. Secondly, it shall also serve the purpose 
of locating the floating roll parallel to the axis of the 
fixed roll. 


5.1.1 It shall consist of an adequately strong fabricated 
steel frame made out of rolled steel sections. 


5.2 Roll Assembly 


One roll shall be fixed while the other shall be of floating 
design. The floating roll shall serve the purposes of: 


a) giving way when any occasional uncrushable 
material fails into the feed opening and thus 
safeguarding the crusher; and 


b) adjustment of the setting of the crusher for 
different applications as well as for compensating 
for the wear and tear of the roll surface. 


5.2.1 The roll assembly shall consist of the shaft, roll 
hub, locking ring, roll shell (or rings or segments 
depending on type and size of roll crusher), bearings 
housed in dust-proof labyrinth rings with greasing 
arrangements for labyrinths and bearings. 


5.2.2 The roll shaft shall be of forged or rolled alloy 
steel, or medium carbon steel, running in self-aligning 
heavy-duty spherical or taper roller bearings. The roll 
hub shall be of cast iron or cast steel. The wearing roll 
tyre shall be of suitable wear-resistant alloy steel. 


5.2.3 The roll width may be varying from 0:66 to 
3-0 times the roll diameter depending upon the capacity 
of the crusher. 


5.3 Drive Unit 


The drive to roll crusher will be such that all the rolls 
will be individually driven or through suitable gears 
or pneumatic tyres. The prime mover may be an 
electric motor, flameproof or non-flame proof as per 
requirement. 


IS 9309 : 2022 


5.3.1 Power developed and transmitted by the power 
unit shall be adequate for the duty to be performed. The 
power unit shall conform to relevant Indian Standard. 


5.4 Cover 


The purpose of the cover is to minimize dust nuisance 
and is to guide the feed material into the roll cavity 
through the sidelines, which shall also minimize 
spillage. 


5.4.1 The cover shall consist of the number of 
suitably welded sections fitted with at least two 
numbers of inspection windows. The sections shall 
be bolted together to permit easy dismantling during 
maintenance. The cover shall be suitably secured to 
the base frame by means of a rapid lock mechanism. 


5.5 Roll Gap Adjustment and Safety Device 


The roll gap shall be adjusted by moving the floating 
roll either towards or away from the stationary roll. 
This setting shall be adjustable by means of operating 
a hand wheel or similar device so located to permit 
easy operation. The adjustment shall be possible by 
keeping the floating roll axis parallel to the fixed roll 
axis. 


5.5.1 The roll crusher shall be equipped with a 
safety device for protecting the crusher against any 
occasional uncrushable material entering the crusher. 
This shall be achieved by providing either a shear pin 
or a breaker bolt or spring loading attachment, which 
yields. 


5.5.2 Heavy duty roll crushers shall be provided with 
either single or combination of truncated cone springs 
or both annular springs ensuring damped recoil; or 
with hydraulic springs. Soon after the removal of 
uncrushable foreign matter, the springs shall regain 
their original prefixed position. 


5.5.3 The above two arrangements, that is roll gap 
adjustment or overload safety shall be either grouped 
together in one device or arranged separately. 


5.6 Feeding and Discharge Chutes 


Depending upon the individual requirement, a suitable 
individual requirement, a suitable feeding device may 
be incorporated. Special consideration needs to be 
given to the height of drop of material and uniform 
feeding across the entire width of the rolls. Incorrect 
attention in this respect may have an unfavourable 
effect on throughput and may result in uneven wear of 
roll surfaces. 


5.6.1 Where required, depending upon the 
understanding between manufacturer and purchaser, 
suitable discharge chutes shall be given. 


5.6.2 Suitable flange connections at the feeding and 
discharge sides shall be given. 


IS 9309 : 2022 


5.7 Attachment for Maintenance of Rolls 


In order to maintain the roll surfaces properly, either 
the rolls have to be built up by welding or by grinding 
corrugation, if any, which develops on smooth roll 
surfaces during crushing may have to be removed. 
The following attachment may have to be procured in 
consultation with the manufacturer. 


5.7.1 To build up the roll surface by welding, the 
manufacturer will offer a suitable kit where required by 
the purchaser. 


5.7.1.1 In the case of smooth roll crushers, where 
required by the purchaser, the manufacturer shall 
provide a suitable grinding attachment to remove the 
possible corrugations that may have taken place during 
crushing. The attachment shall be such that both the 
rolls are face milled simultaneously in a single work 
cycle. The operation will be such that longitudinal 
movement of the attachment shall be automatic with 
the only feed out being given manually. 


5.7.1.2 Alternatively, where required, a suitable 
arrangement may be given on one of the rolls for axial 
shifting of the same to remove corrugation. 


6 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 


6.1 Safety Requirements 


The design of the crusher shall minimize hazards to 
the operator. All gears, pulleys, chains, belt sprockets, 
dangerous moving parts and parts that are subject to 
high operating temperatures or are energized electrically 
shall be insulated, well-guarded and protected. 


6.2 The roll shall be housed suitably in dust-proof 
covers and if required by the purchaser, a suitable 
flange connection for the dust extraction system may 
be incorporated. Similarly, if required by the purchaser, 
the machine may be mounted on vibration mounts to 
dampen the crusher vibrations. 


6.3 To facilitate changing of rolls and for conducting 
maintenance work on the crusher, if required by the 
purchaser, the crusher may be provided with collapsible 
wheels, so that the crusher can be brought out of the 
feeding chute. 


6.4 Maintenance Accessibility 


The design of the crusher shall provide convenient 
access to all components, sub-assemblies and parts for 
maintenance and repairs. 


6.5 Lubrication 


Lubrication means shall be provided for the bearings 
and other parts requiring lubrication. All lubricating 
nipples shall be of a similar type, preferably located 
centrally with properly arranged grease or oil pipes. 
Lubrication points shall be conspicuously marked to 


identify them. Chains shall be enclosed, and where 
standard reduction gearboxes are used, the same shall 
conform to relevant Indian Standard. 


6.6 Automatic greasing station may be provided if 
required by the purchaser. 


6.7 Where the crusher is used for crushing hot materials, 
suitable cooling arrangements for shafts and bearings 
shall be provided. 


6.8 Maintenance Tools and Manual 

A strong toolbox with lock and key containing the 
special and normal tools for maintaining the roll crusher 
together with instruction and maintenance manual shall 
be provided. The toolbox shall be suitably affixed to 
the machine. 


7 DESIGNATION 


The designation of roll crusher shall include: 


a) Commonly used name; 
b) Number of rolls; 


c) Type of roll surface — S = smooth, B = beaded, 
T = toothed and C = corrugated; 


d) Roll diameter in millimetres; 
e) Roll rpm or peripheral speed...m/s; 
f) Roll width in millimetres; and 
g) Number of this standard. 
Example: 


A roll crusher comprising of two smooth rolls of diameter 
1000 mm and width 1200 mm be designated as Double Roll 
Crusher, Types S, 1000 x 1200 mm, IS 9303 


8 SUPPLY 


The manufacturer shall supply a certificate to the 
purchaser along with each machine certifying that the 
crusher has been inspected for freedom from visible 
defects and the crusher has satisfactorily withstood 
the trial run. Items to be covered under this certificate 
are given in Annex C. The purchaser may inspect the 
machine during and after fabrication. 


8.1 Crusher shall generally meet the application data 
provided by the purchaser and agreed to by the supplier. 


8.2 For large crushers, a load test shall be conducted at 
the purchaser’s end. 


9 MARKING PLATE 


9.1 Each machine shall have a plate firmly attached to it 
clearly visible and not easily removable. The plate shall 
have marked on it the following information: 

a) Manufacturer’s name and address or trademark; 


b) Manufacturer’s reference/model number of the 
machine; 


c) Type of machine (see 7); and 
d) Month and Year of manufacture. 
9.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this Standard may be certified as per the conformity 


IS 9309 : 2022 


assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


IS 9309 : 2022 


ANNEX A 
( Foreword ) 


INFORMATION TO BE SUPPLIED BY THE PURCHASER TO 
THE MANUFACTURER WITH THE ENQUIRY AND ORDER 


A-1 The enquiry and order should state: 
a) Description of feed material to be crushed; 
b) Bulk density in kg/m? of feed material; 
c) Condition of feed material (dusty, moist, hard, 


d) Structure of feed material (crystalline or granular 
or slabby); 


e) Crushing strength (work index, flakiness index, 
elongation index); 


f) Size range of feed material in mm; and 


medium-hard, soft, clean, dirty). If moist, 

percentage of moisture; g) Duty (continuous or intermittent). 
ANNEX B 
( Foreword ) 


INFORMATION TO BE FURNISHED BY THE MANUFACTURER TO THE PURCHASER ALONG 
WITH THE QUOTATION AND SUPPLY 


B-1 The manufacturer shall give the following 
information along with his quotation and supply: 


a) Size and designation of roll crusher; 

b) Maximum feed size in millimetres; 

c) Minimum and maximum size of discharge in 
millimetres with guaranteed sieve analysis; 

d) Capacity in tonne per hour mentioning the bulk 
density taken into consideration; 


e) Power requirements at the output of motor/prime 
mover shaft in kW; 


f) Details of crusher underlying the materials 
of construction type and size of important 
components, such as shafts, roll hub, rolls and 
bearings, drive units, roll gap adjustment and 
safety devices, etc.; 


g) Expected product analysis at different settings; 
h) Normal expected life; 


j) List of recommended spares for 2 years of normal 
operation; and 

k) General arrangement drawing giving overall 
dimensions, foundation plan and loading size and 
details of input and output flanges. 


ANNEX C 
(Clause 8 ) 


INFORMATION TO BE GIVEN IN THE CERTIFICATE BY THE MANUFACTURER TO THE 
PURCHASER AT THE TIME OF SUPPLYING THE MACHINE 


C-1 INSPECTION 


The inspection report shall state that each part of the 
crusher has been inspected before painting to ensure 
that it is free from any visible defects in casting, 
machining, etc. 


C-2 TEST RUN 
The test run report shall state the following: 


a) The number of hours the crusher has been run 
continuously under no-load after completion of 
the assembly; and 


b) That after dismantling the crusher consequent to 
the trial run, inspection has been carried out to 
ensure that: 


1) the construction of the 
satisfactory; 


crusher is 


2) lubricating condition is satisfactory; 


3) there is no slackness or unusual wear on any 
component; and 


4) the bearings are evenly loaded. 


IS 9309 : 2022 


ANNEX D 
( Foreword )

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
